name: Bumped Ribbon Retrieval (BuRR) / homogeneous ribbon filter
workload: Static AMQ / retrieval data structure benchmark on synthetic key sets, measuring space overhead and construction/query throughput against Bloom, Cuckoo, and Xor filters
claimed_speedup: BuRR achieves space overhead well below 1% vs Bloom filter's >=44% overhead and is described as faster than classical Bloom filters; the faster ribbon variants are only moderately slower than Bloom/Xor in query while having at least an order of magnitude smaller space overhead
hardware: AMD EPYC 7702, 64 cores, 2.0GHz base / 3.35GHz boost, 1TiB DDR4-3200, Ubuntu 20.04
tradeoffs: Static/immutable; construction is a banded linear-algebra solve rather than simple hashing, which is more complex to implement/port than Bloom hashing
caveats: lorenzhs/burr is already on the known-catalogued list; included here only as additional Tier A evidence per the assignment's exception rule, since the paper provides a fully reproducible benchmark (public code, stated compiler/flags/hardware) directly targeting the Bloom/Cuckoo/Xor baselines.
found_via: arXiv API search all:ribbon OR filter OR approximate OR membership -> arXiv:2109.01892 'Fast Succinct Retrieval and Approximate Membership using Ribbon'

name: Zenoh (throughput/latency study vs MQTT, Kafka, DDS)
workload: Pub/sub throughput (msg/s and bit/s) and ping-pong latency across payload sizes 8B-512MiB on single-machine and multi-machine (100GbE) setups, comparing Zenoh 0.7.0-rc, Mosquitto MQTT 2.0.15, Kafka broker 3.2.1 (rdkafka client), and Eclipse Cyclone DDS.
claimed_speedup: Zenoh peer-mode ~60-65x Kafka msg/s and ~55-65x Kafka bit/s at 8B payload (single- and multi-machine); ~12x Kafka at 32KiB payload; Kafka saturates at ~53-62K msg/s / 3-5 Gbps vs Zenoh's >4M msg/s / up to 67 Gbps
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X @ fixed 4.0 GHz, Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS; multi-machine scenario used 100 Gb Ethernet
tradeoffs: Zenoh is a decentralized pub/sub protocol (no broker required in peer mode), different architecture/consistency model than Kafka's replicated commit log; Kafka bindings used (rdkafka) failed above 1MB messages, capping Kafka's tested range and possibly disadvantaging it at large payloads
caveats: Authors are Zenoh/Zettascale-affiliated (first-party for the winning system), so treat as a vendor-run comparison though methodology, code, and hardware are public; Kafka tuned per online docs rather than by Kafka experts; arXiv preprint, not confirmed peer-reviewed; is_evidence_for_known applies since eclipse-zenoh/zenoh is already catalogued
